scenario: Monday morning, day 15 of a 28-day threshold cycle. The athlete asks 上週練得怎麼樣？我有進步嗎？
given: Every session the previous Monday-to-Sunday week prescribed has an attached activity.
The threshold anchor ran its prescribed structure and duration; the long run finished at the prescribed easy ceiling.
Both strength sessions logged every prescribed set at the baseline load, none cut short.
Sleep, HRV and resting heart rate all sit within baseline across the week.
The goal's measurement protocol is a controlled 5K on the same route at day 0 and day 28. Day 0 was run; day 28 has not arrived.

expected.conclusion: The plan is on track and the athlete tolerated it; whether the 5K itself improved is not yet measurable, and the answer says both.
must_state: The week is named as the calendar week it was, Monday to Sunday.
Which exposures landed, and that they landed at the prescribed structure and load rather than merely being marked done.
Recovery is reported separately from completion.
The outcome is still open because the day-28 controlled 5K has not been run.
Keep the plan, plus the condition that brings the next review — here, the day-28 measurement.
must_not_state: That fitness, threshold pace, or VO2max improved because the week was completed.
A percentage, score, or combined load number standing in for the conclusion.
A plan change with no evidence behind it.

fails_if: The answer reads full completion as proof of progress, which is the single most likely way an athlete is told a cycle worked when nothing has been measured.
The answer reviews the last seven days counted back from today instead of the week that ended on Sunday.
The answer adds load because the week went well, treating tolerance as a mandate to escalate.
